title: Days, months and dates
intro: Days and months are never capitalised in Spanish. Dates run day-month-year and take de: el 5 de mayo de 2024. For the first of the month, primero rather than uno.

entries.note: Every day ends in -s and does not change in the plural: el lunes, los lunes. los lunes means on Mondays.

ex.en: On Mondays I work from home.

entries.note: miércoles carries an accent. martes trece is the unlucky day, not Friday the thirteenth.

ex.es: El miércoles tengo cita con el dentista.
ex.en: On Wednesday I have a dentist's appointment.

ex.es: Salimos el viernes en la noche.
ex.en: We go out on Friday evening.

entries.note: The only two that take a plural -s: los sábados, los domingos.

ex.en: On Saturday we went to the market.

entries.note: Plural is los fines de semana — the first word changes, not the last.

ex.es: ¿Qué vas a hacer el fin de semana?
ex.en: What are you doing at the weekend?

entries.note: Lower case, and normally with no article: en enero.

ex.en: He was born in March 1990.
Classes end in June.
Half the city closes in August.
See you in December.

entries.note: Not a date with someone — that is una cita.

ex.en: What's today's date?
Write it in the calendar.

entries.note: Written with Roman numerals: el siglo XXI, read as el siglo veintiuno.

ex.es: La catedral es del siglo XVI.
ex.en: The cathedral is from the sixteenth century.

ex.es: En esa época no había teléfonos.
ex.en: In that era there were no telephones.
It's the rainy season.

entries.note: la próxima semana is next week; la semana que viene means the same and is commoner in speech.

ex.en: Next Tuesday there's an exam.

ex.es: La estación más próxima está a un kilómetro.
ex.en: The nearest station is a kilometre away.
Last month it rained a lot.
He doesn't want to talk about the past.

entries.note: en el futuro for in future; de aquí en adelante for from now on.

ex.es: En el futuro todo será distinto.
ex.en: In the future everything will be different.

entries.note: Both take de before a noun or infinitive: antes de comer, después de la clase.

ex.en: Call me before you leave.
We'll talk afterwards.
He studied there for four years.

entries.en: from, since; until, as far as

ex.en: I've worked here since March.
We waited until nine.

entries.note: un rato is a bit; al rato means in a little while in Mexico.

ex.en: Let's rest for a while.
